description: Numeric literals that commonly appear unexplained in code, with named Fraction replacements and a falsifies_if condition for each.

entries.falsifies_if: an invariant uses 0.5 as a float literal instead of Fraction(1, 2) in arithmetic.
an invariant uses a decimal approximation of one-third.
an invariant uses a decimal approximation of two-thirds.
an invariant uses 0.25 as a float literal.
an invariant uses 0.75 as a float literal.
an invariant uses 0.1 as a float literal (IEEE-754 loses precision).
an invariant uses 0.01 as a float literal.
a financial invariant uses 0.0001 as a float literal.
a reliability invariant uses 0.99999 as a float literal.
a statistics invariant uses 0.95 as a float literal.
a reliability invariant uses 0.99 as a float literal.
an aesthetic invariant uses the float approximation of phi.
entries.context: aesthetic ratio; prefer the exact algebraic definition when available

entries.falsifies_if: a numerical invariant uses 2.71828 as a float literal.
entries.context: Euler number approximation; prefer series evaluation

entries.falsifies_if: a geometric invariant uses 3.14159 as a float literal.
entries.context: pi; prefer Machin-like series or arc-length integral
